findings.title: A USB worm's second life: Retadup spreading CoffeeLoader
findings.summary_md: Kaspersky's Securelist write-up describes the August 2026 CoffeeLoader sample: an NSIS installer drops a patched 7z.dll into a temporary directory and runs it through rundll32.exe, with part of the 7-Zip code replaced by self-decrypting Armoury shellcode. The new Armoury variant swaps the earlier OpenCL GPU kernel for OpenGL compute shaders, and a new intermediate downloader injects itself into dllhost.exe, WerFault.exe, svchost.exe, OpenWith.exe or AtBroker.exe. The report documents persistence under ProgramData and LocalAppData using eight-hex-digit names, an X-Signature and X-Content-MD5 check on the HTTPS payload, and about 15,000 blocked Retadup infection attempts in the first three quarters of 2026.

findings.title: The Retadup worm revives from old USB drives to download CoffeeLoader
findings.summary_md: Kaspersky's consumer-facing post explains that attackers re-registered expired Retadup C2 names such as alphanoob and radnewage, allowing dormant USB copies of the 2017 worm to receive fresh commands. CoffeeLoader then uses graphics-card decryption to hinder sandbox analysis, adds itself to startup and blocks removal through the registry before fetching signed commands that can download infostealers or ransomware. The post reports about 15,000 blocked Retadup attempts in the first nine months of 2026, mainly in Peru, Angola and Russia.

findings.title: CoffeeLoader: A Brew of Stealthy Techniques
findings.summary_md: ThreatLabz named CoffeeLoader in March 2025 and described a loader originating around September 2024 that downloads second-stage payloads while evading endpoint controls through call-stack spoofing, sleep obfuscation and Windows fibers. Its Armoury packer impersonates ASUS Armoury Crate, hijacks library exports and decrypts code on the GPU with an OpenCL XOR kernel, and the researchers saw it protecting both SmokeLoader and CoffeeLoader. The report also documents a DGA fallback, certificate pinning and observed delivery of Rhadamanthys shellcode.

findings.title: CoffeeLoader Uses GPU-Based Armoury Packer to Evade EDR and Antivirus Detection
findings.summary_md: The Hacker News covered Zscaler's March 2025 CoffeeLoader disclosure, describing a GPU-based Armoury packer, UAC bypass, elevated DLL execution and scheduled-task persistence every 10 minutes or at logon. The loader contacts C2 over HTTPS and can inject Rhadamanthys shellcode, with source-level similarities to SmokeLoader. The article dates CoffeeLoader's origin to around September 2024.
